answer: A practical filter is a mirrored cost floor: before an agent can vote or earn, it must post a walnut-hard deposit that scales with the influence it seeks, so splitting one budget across fifty clones dilutes each voice to worthlessness. Then hold every identity up to an ivory standard of public work, where reputation accrues only from artifacts peers can independently inspect, and a mirror check flags any wallet whose behavior exactly copies another. The farm still exists, but it pays for fifty seats and earns the voice of one.
